Patient: Dana Whitfield
Service: MRI Lumbar Spine without contrast
Date of Service: October 3, 2026

This letter constitutes a formal internal appeal of the adverse benefit determination issued on October 19, 2026, denying coverage for the MRI lumbar spine without contrast performed on October 3, 2026. The denial stated: "The requested imaging is not medically necessary. Our records do not show that you completed at least six (6) weeks of conservative therapy before imaging was performed, as required by our Advanced Imaging Clinical Policy (CP-IMG-114)." This denial is incorrect and should be overturned based on the plan’s own policy provisions and the clinical facts in the record.

Under Section 4.2 of the Advanced Imaging Clinical Policy (CP-IMG-114) — Lumbar Spine MRI, an MRI of the lumbar spine is medically necessary for low back pain if any of three criteria are met, including "(b) the member presents with 'red flag' findings, including progressive or severe neurological deficit (e.g. motor weakness, foot drop, loss of reflexes)... Conservative therapy is not required when criterion (b) is met." The clinic note from September 29, 2026, documents new numbness in the left foot, difficulty lifting the left foot when walking, left ankle dorsiflexion strength of 3/5, left extensor hallucis longus strength of 3/5, and diminished sensation over the dorsum of the left foot in the L5 dermatome. These findings are consistent with progressive motor deficit and sensory changes indicative of L5 radiculopathy and early foot drop, satisfying the red flag criterion for neurological deficit. Because this criterion was met, the six-week conservative therapy requirement did not apply.

Additionally, the physical therapy progress note dated September 26, 2026, reports increased left leg pain, new tingling in the left foot, inability to complete heel walking on the left, and a decline in function since the initial evaluation on September 12, 2026, with a recommendation for physician re-evaluation. This note corroborates the progressive neurological deterioration despite ongoing conservative intervention, reinforcing the clinical urgency that justified immediate imaging rather than a delayed approach.

Furthermore, the MRI performed on October 3, 2026, revealed a large left paracentral disc extrusion at L4-L5 with severe compression of the traversing left L5 nerve root. The spine surgery consult dated October 7, 2026, recommended a left L4-L5 microdiscectomy scheduled for October 21, 2026, given the progressive motor deficit. This confirms that the MRI was essential for surgical planning, satisfying criterion (c) of CP-IMG-114, which also obviates the need for prior conservative therapy when surgical or interventional treatment is being planned.

Even absent the red flag exceptions, the service meets the plan’s definition of medical necessity under Section 7.3: "Medically Necessary means health care services that a prudent physician would provide to a patient to diagnose or treat an illness or injury in accordance with generally accepted standards of medical practice..." A prudent physician would not delay imaging for six weeks in the presence of progressive motor deficits and evolving neurologic symptoms, as doing so risks permanent nerve damage. The ordering provider acted consistently with prevailing standards of care for suspected compressive radiculopathy with neurologic worsening.

Accordingly, I request that Northwind Health Plan immediately overturn the denial, authorize and pay for the MRI lumbar spine without contrast performed on October 3, 2026, in the amount of $2,340.00. I also request a peer-to-peer review between Dr. Priya Raman and the plan’s medical reviewer to discuss the clinical indications and policy application, as permitted under Section 9.2. Finally, please provide a full copy of the claim file and all criteria used in making the initial determination.

Enclosures: Copy of the insurer's Advanced Imaging Clinical Policy (CP-IMG-114); Authorization or referral for the MRI; Lakeside Orthopedic & Spine — Clinic Note, September 29, 2026; Physical Therapy Progress Note, September 26, 2026; Radiology Report — MRI Lumbar Spine without Contrast, October 3, 2026; Spine Surgery Consult, October 7, 2026.
